implementationPlan: The run first normalized the URL-shortener requirement, then established an architecture and API contract. Core link creation, persistence and redirect handling were implemented alongside asynchronous click analytics. Unit and integration tests were added before the reviewer compiled the generated project and executed the test suite. Risk assessment and the final engineering summary complete the workflow.
rationale: The decomposition establishes architecture contracts before implementation, allows independent core and analytics work, separates unit and integration validation, and places deterministic build validation before the final engineering summary.
risksAndTradeoffs: The reference implementation uses a single H2 database and therefore does not provide production multi-region availability.
The local cache improves hot redirect reads but is process-local.
Analytics is asynchronous and best effort, so queue saturation can result in dropped events.
Unauthenticated link creation and sequential short codes require additional abuse and enumeration controls for internet-scale deployment.
validationApproach: The reviewer materializes the generated source and tests into an isolated reference workspace, runs Maven compilation first, then executes the JUnit test suite and records the result as validation evidence. Unit tests cover core validation and click recording while integration tests exercise H2 persistence, analytics aggregation and HTTP redirects.
assumptions: The implementation is a single deployable Java service.
H2 represents the relational persistence boundary for the reference implementation.
Authentication, link expiry and multi-region deployment remain outside this iteration.
limitations: No production-grade distributed database or cache is included.
No authentication, rate limiting or abuse-prevention service is implemented.
No multi-region active-active deployment is implemented.
The reference HTTP implementation uses the JDK HttpServer rather than a production web framework.
